saints.name: St. André Bessette
saints.title: Religious
saints.shortBlurb: A humble Holy Cross brother and doorkeeper whose devotion to St. Joseph drew a wounded world to his door…
biography: Born in 1845 at Saint-Grégoire d'Iberville in Quebec and orphaned at twelve, Alfred Bessette was frail in body and nearly without schooling. In 1870 he was received into the Congregation of Holy Cross as Brother André and assigned as porter of Notre-Dame College in Montreal, a post he kept some forty years, joking that his superiors had shown him the door and he had stayed there.

At that door the sick found him, and thousands came; he prayed with them and pointed them to Saint Joseph, and many reported cures, which he ascribed wholly to the intercession of the foster father of Jesus. The Miracle Man of Montreal, people called him, and from the alms of the grateful he raised on Mount Royal the first chapel of what became Saint Joseph's Oratory.

Brother André died on 6 January 1937, aged ninety-one, and a million mourners filed past his coffin in the winter cold. Beatified by Pope John Paul II in 1982, he was canonized by Pope Benedict XVI on 17 October 2010, the first saint of the Congregation of Holy Cross. Because of the cures at his door he is honored as a patron of the sick.
saints.knownFor: His devotion to St. Joseph and the Oratory on Mount Royal.
